garment.name: waist-band
garment.title: waist-band
garment.reason: A long woven red cotton waist-band with pink/green wool decoration, consistent with Otavalo woven belts (faja) worn in Andean Ecuador dress; museum attributes it directly to Otavalo makers.

garment.name: klänning
garment.title: klänning
garment.reason: A girl's white cotton dress with pale-blue floral embroidery around the neckline and sleeves, labeled by the collecting museum as Otavalo (Imbabura, Ecuador) girl's dress; this matches known Otavalo children's/women's embroidered blouse-dress traditions.

garment.name: sjal
garment.title: sjal
garment.reason: A white embroidered wool shawl (sjal) with a colorful embroidered border, identified as belonging to Otavalo traditional dress from Imbabura, Ecuador — consistent with the claimed garment and ethnicity.

garment.name: hatt, Filthatt., hat
garment.title: hatt, Filthatt., hat
garment.reason: A white felt hat (filthatt) attributed to Otavalo, Imbabura, Ecuador per museum documentation — this type of felt hat is a traditional accessory worn by Otavalo men and women.

garment.name: toffel, Tofflor.
garment.title: toffel, Tofflor.
garment.reason: The image shows a pair of handwoven striped textile slippers collected in Otavalo, Imbabura, Ecuador — consistent with Otavalo footwear/garment craft.

garment.name: waist-band
garment.title: waist-band
garment.reason: A long woven cotton waist-band (faja) with pink, yellow, and white banding and tassels, attributed by the museum to Otavalo makers — this is a traditional Andean belt type consistent with Otavalo dress.

photo.name: Otavalointiaaninainen  kantamassa isoa ruukkua selässään.
photo.title: Otavalointiaaninainen  kantamassa isoa ruukkua selässään.
photo.reason: A woman in traditional dress and hat carries a large jar on her back at San Pablo lagoon near Otavalo, Ecuador — a documentary photo of Otavalo daily life and dress.

jewelry.name: smycke, halsband
jewelry.title: smycke, halsband
jewelry.reason: Multi-strand necklace of small gold-colored glass beads, bought at the Otavalo market and documented as made/worn by the Otavalo people — a classic item of Otavalo dress adornment.

jewelry.name: nål
jewelry.title: nål
jewelry.reason: This is a metal pin with a decorative glass-set head, described as a "nål" used to fasten the shawl of Otavalo dress (tupu-type pin), collected in Imbabura, Ecuador. This matches a garment accessory used by the Otavalo people.

jewelry.name: halsband, smycke
jewelry.title: halsband, smycke
jewelry.reason: A four-strand necklace of large gold-colored glass beads, purchased at the Otavalo market and matching the well-known Otavalo gold-bead necklace tradition worn by Otavaleña women.

jewelry.name: smycke, Snöre
jewelry.title: smycke, Snöre
jewelry.reason: Strands of red glass beads purchased at the Otavalo market, Ecuador—a necklace type characteristic of Otavalo women's traditional dress (coral-red glass bead necklaces, "huallcas").

instruments.name: panflöjt
instruments.title: panflöjt
instruments.reason: A bamboo panpipe purchased in the Otavalo market, consistent with Andean panpipes used by Otavalo and neighboring Andean peoples in Imbabura, Ecuador.

textile.name: väv, band, fabric, tira
textile.title: väv, band, fabric, tira
textile.reason: This is a handwoven patterned band (faja/belt-type trim) in blue and white geometric design, collected directly from Otavalo, Ecuador, consistent with Otavalo weaving traditions.
